title: The First Called · Through the Gate
dek: Cala and Nuru summon strangers against Death, then flee. The first company must survive the forest, find shelter and learn what it means to make Prima home.

facts.People: Jiangshi; Adelia; Scribonia; Gartina; Jako; Quake; Forgax; Empty; John; Keno; Force; Azeran; Melian Starguard; the early company
facts.Outcome: The company reaches shelter; the Gate closes and the settlement’s defense becomes shared work

body:
The first Called stepped through the Gate on 4, Month of War, Year 1: Day 1 of the Final War. Cala and Nuru warned of Death and the Wyrm, then vanished when they believed the danger had found them. Before reaching the promised settlement, they would lose the gods’ guidance, fight creatures rising from the forest floor and see the portal close behind them.

Pristinia was still a small community finding its name. The company’s first days made the appeal to save a world tangible: keep danger off the road, help the injured, and become useful to the people already living there.

The portal stirs

Gartina came through with half an apple in her mouth and the sudden realization that her pie was still in the oven. Scribonia stepped carefully into the clearing, holding a heavy book and a crystal. Jiangshi could barely keep herself in the air. Adelia emerged from the shadows surprised to be free of her prison. Around them stood strangers who had brought different languages, loyalties and expectations into the same forest.

Cala’s radiance and Nuru’s dusk met above the forgotten portal. When the light faded, their avatars stood before the arrivals: a strong, luminous woman and a ruined-looking man. Quake saluted. Jako hesitated, struggling to put questions into spoken words. Empty asked the question that the spectacle had not answered: why were they here?

Nuru told them they had been called to defy Death, who sought the end of everything. Cala spoke of the Wyrm of the World’s End consuming life and light. Neither could offer a way to kill it. When John asked, Cala said they were feeding its hunger until it slept, slowing an advance they could not stop. That was the gods’ account. The newcomers could ask questions, but had little means yet to test the answers.

The reactions were their own. Adelia accepted the challenge eagerly. Quake promised to do what he could. Gartina protested the thought of a world without sunsets, food and ordinary pleasures. Scribonia asked about the laws of magic. Their agreement to help did not mean they understood the same task.

A warning without a plan

The gods directed them toward a small settlement on Prima. Nuru described the island as a haven where they could find their footing while the war continued. Jako wanted to know whether they would have a home there. Cala assured them that one was ready. Empty could offer his fists; Nuru answered that he might become more than he yet imagined. Gartina’s answer to the scale of the danger was to find more friends.

Adelia was already investigating. The shadows among the trees felt cold, and fungus grew where she touched them. She took a sample on her dagger. It was lifeless. When she held it up to Nuru, he went pale and urged Cala to leave: he believed Death had found them.

Their instructions ended in a hurry. Cala had left a talisman by a tree. She warned the company to use it only when they needed truth, because truth carried a cost. Then both avatars vanished in a flash. The forest went quiet. Keno asked whether anyone had obtained directions to the village.

No god remained beside them to choose the road or fight what was coming. They had a promised refuge, an unexplained object, and warnings whose urgency they had only just begun to understand.

What Quake could see

Scribonia found the talisman protected from the strange growth. It was a simple sword bearing an ancient rune. He recognized the meaning as a harsh kind of truth and cautioned the others. Forgax disliked being ordered to help decipher it, though he offered his aid. Their rivalry had survived the crossing intact.

Quake refused to leave the blade behind. Taking its hilt made him sick and changed what he saw. He saw faded color and a decaying landscape hidden from the others. He could discern remnants of divine power and beings rising beneath the ground. To the others, the warning arrived first through his words.

Keno noticed the fungal mounds moving. Empty felt a tremor. Jiangshi rose toward the trees to look for the settlement, while Quake led the company toward the road. Soon the beings Quake had sensed inhabited the fungus and burst out as corpse-like creatures. They had come to consume the gods’ remaining power; seeing other magical life, they turned toward the adventurers.

Quake put himself between the creatures and the company. They could not simply run toward the promised village and bring the attack with them. His warning gave them time to ready themselves before the first blows.

Strangers holding a line

Scribonia lifted Jako onto his shoulders so their shorter stride would not leave them behind. Jako sent roots into the ground to restrain the attackers. Keno moved beside Quake to shield the smaller companions. John and Jiangshi watched from the air. Gartina, who had arrived dressed for gardening, used edible glitter to mark a target and threw stones she had intended for soup.

The corpses would not reliably stay down. One fell beneath Jiangshi’s magic and rose again; another broke free after Forgax struck it. The companions called for fire and began burning what they could. Scribonia fought while keeping Jako clear of the danger. Forgax deflected a blow with a magical barrier. Cooperation was something they had to do before they had finished deciding what they thought of one another.

A shadow appeared among the trees near Keno, mocking Adelia’s account of her own nature. Its arguments remained the creature’s taunts, not a settled definition of every shadow in Fenumion. John brought it down, but its remnants entered him. He was left contaminated by Death.

Adelia fell and rose again amid the fighting. Jiangshi offered healing, while Gartina, standing nearby, applied a family mixture that smelled like a beef rub. The danger had not put an end to Gartina’s practical absurdity. As the shadow’s strength faded, the remaining corpses became easier to destroy. Limbs dropped away and turned to dust; a remnant of Cala’s radiance stopped one from rising.

Before the battle was quite over, the portal rippled shut. Two figures had been seen struggling inside it. Their passage did not complete in the scene. Jako wondered whether the company had been meant to keep the way open. Gartina feared no more help would come. The record establishes that closure, not the identities or eventual fate of the figures caught beyond it.

A settlement already living

With the attack spent, the company gathered the bodies for burning and checked who still needed help. Quake set down the sword. Handling it had exacted a physical cost, and Forgax eventually took it, insisting that he could choose for himself. Scribonia wanted access to study it. John described what he had absorbed to protect Keno and said a watching face had appeared among the trees. Scribonia could not see that watcher; his suggestion that divine magic might help remained a suggestion.

The road narrowed into a canyon. At a fork, Scribonia spotted an ambush on one route and a concealed path along a stream on the other. He stopped the company and led them away from the danger. Clouds and fog covered their passage. They had survived the clearing without thereby making every road safe.

Beyond the canyon lay a lake and the settlement. Quake searched for a way across, then walked around. The others followed toward wooden homes, chimney smoke, lanterns and people going about their lives. Forgax still saw a disturbing dark shape that the rest could not, another reminder that their knowledge of the new land was uneven.

The settlement’s people, houses and history preceded the newcomers. That evening it gave the company somewhere to recover, and people whose safety their next decisions would affect.

Something to offer one another

Jiangshi had been exhausted before the fight began. After reaching the settlement, she offered cherry-blossom tea. Gartina volunteered scones. Quake accepted the chance to sit quietly; Jako watched the ceremony with curiosity and searched for the right words of thanks.

Jiangshi laid out her cups and turned each one before offering it. She carried a cup to Adelia, who had withdrawn to write about the battle and her companions’ abilities. Adelia accepted and stayed to know the others better. For a little while the newcomers could offer something besides weapons and warnings.

Then Jiangshi’s strength gave out and she fainted. Adelia watched over her. John still carried the contamination from the fight, and the company needed rest.

The road beyond the welcome

In the following days, Melian Starguard asked the arrivals to clear the roads to the portal. Her people could turn back ordinary bandits, she said, but her guards had fled from the undead. They lacked training and equipment. She could not accompany the expedition because that would leave the settlement unprotected.

Gartina proposed food, training and a smithy as parts of the answer. Claire considered the injured people a scouting party might bring back and arranged for her daughter to stay behind. Quake pledged himself to the land and its people. Melian hoped warriors like him might teach her guards to defend their own home. Gartina could provide meals; others would have to teach and equip the guards.

The town’s name was not settled at the first crossing. Melian called it the Homestead and described a shelter for wanderers. Later, she invited the adventurers to help choose something more permanent. Adelia suggested a darker name; Scribonia wanted an optimistic one. Jiangshi proposed Pristinia. Melian liked it as an aspiration, and resisted John’s grander addition to the name. Scribonia and John supported Pristinia; Quake abstained. Melian wrote it across the map.

She then showed them the town in the rain: their imperfect dwellings, Herb’s tavern, and workshops whose business had paused in the cold weather. At the Common Man, Herb offered a free drink. Quake improved the muddy entrance with drainage. A loom, brewery, distillery, tanner, baker and butcher belonged to the place they had been asked to defend. The name on the map now pointed to people and work they were learning to recognize.

What begins here

The later early-arrival accounts preserve more questions. Akarian needed explanations of the war, asked whether such different companions could be trusted, and heard Jako’s remembered experiences through spores. Claire answered part of his unease through the story of her own family. His offer to help teach her daughter remained an offer in that exchange. Forgax’s later scouting toward a pillar visible to him alone likewise belongs to the company’s gradual, uneven discovery of Prima.

Those connected histories do not all occur during the first clearing battle. The first recovered company marks Day 1 of the Final War; the later Third Arrival is a separate event, and neither label is a complete census of everyone who crossed. What began at the portal continued through a closed route, injuries, cups of tea, a town’s naming and promises to protect people the newcomers had only just met.
